title: Understanding Model Bias
text: Model bias refers to the error introduced by approximating a real-world problem, which may be complex, by a simplified model. High bias can occur if the model is too simple to capture the underlying patterns in the data.

title: Role of the Intercept
text: The intercept in a model represents the expected value of the dependent variable when all independent variables are zero. Removing it might affect the model's ability to fit the data properly.

title: Effect of Removing the Intercept
text: What happens to the model's flexibility when the intercept is removed?

title: Impact on Bias
text: Consider how removing the intercept might impact the model's bias. Does it make the model more or less capable of capturing the true relationship between variables?
